To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

out-of-home childhood placement and abuse are related to homelessness in adulthood, that homeless adults with histories of childhood placement or abuse may not be self-actualizing, that the number of homeless episodes may be related to self-actualization, and that the number of episodes of homelessness is related to abuse.
homeless men who had experienced childhood out-of-home placements or abuse reported more episodes of homelessness and had been homeless longer than homeless men without these histories.

homeless men who were in out-of-home placement as a child had a longer time between first episode of homelessness and the current episode, had a longer length of time homeless in the current episode, and had more episodes of homeless than homeless men without out-of-home placement histories; homeless men who experienced abuse in childhood had more episodes of home-lessness than homeless men who did not experience abuse in childhood; and homeless men with a longer length of homelessness in the current episode had lower self-actualization than homeless
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of childhood out-of-place placement and abuse in the etiology of homelessness in men.

a new concept: the cognitive-affective preparation of homelessness.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the homeless men studied were prepared for homelessness by a lack of belonging in childhood and a subsequent inability to form lasting attachments in adult life.
the homeless men in this study had a history of abuse and/or out-of-home placement that influenced the way they prepared for homelessness and their ability to cope with it. (Author/JAC)
the homeless are not a homogenous group and that their experiences in childhood are related to the patterns of homelessness they experience. (Contains 4 tables and 1 figure.)
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
out-of-home placements and abuse are related to preparation for homelessness and are important factors to consider in prevention and intervention.
homelessness is not a single event or a single problem but a complex set of problems and events that may have a cumulative effect over time.

childhood out-of-home placements and child abuse were related to homelessness, but that these relationships were mediated by the need for love and belonging, and by cognitive-affective preparation for adult homelessness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
homelessness is a complex problem with many causes.
the loss of feelings of safety, love and belonging during childhood can lead to a lifetime of homelessness.

homeless men who have had out-of-home placement as children and those who have experienced abuse are more likely to be chronically homeless and that the loss of feelings of love and belonging in childhood is preparatory for adult homelessness.
